items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Look! A sea swallow!
Avgust holds a half-crumpled paper plane over his head, imitating a bird in flight.
All those unsent letters, just the same as any other waste paper—the building materials for folding birds and frogs.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: That's not right. You shouldn't fold it this way.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Use these math papers to make dotted frogs—the ones that can jump if you flick them.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But we already have so many frogs.

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: No fighting!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I wasn't! I'm just saying he used the wrong paper.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: It's ok, Pasono, we still have lots of paper.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: These seem nice. They aren't too crumply.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Comrade Avgust, use this.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Thank you, Comrade Nina! I think this sea swallow will do just fine.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: It's a little crumpled and looks a bit dirty, but these battle scars are like medals for a hero, just like the one that saved our town.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I want to show it to Vila.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila—
Before his friends could answer, Avgust is in a full sprint toward the adults on the other end of the corridor.
Noticing his coming, Vila opens her arms, but her duty as a teacher overrides her welcome.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Don't run in the corridor, Comrade Avgust.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What's wrong?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Look! This is my sea swallow!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: It has been in many battles and flown for a long, long way. It's very tired and wants some rest.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: So, I want it to rest here with you.
The crumpled paper plane lands in Vila's palm.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Oh, thank you, Comrade Avgust.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It will be treated the way a heroic sea swallow deserves, I promise.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Ok!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What do you think? Perhaps it might like to rest in this notebook?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Just like this. Sleep tight, little hero.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Since you're here, Comrade Avgust. I must confirm with you: are you all prepared to go to the SPDM?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I don't understand. What do we need to prepare?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You must have all the things you want to take with you and study your schedule so you will know where to go.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Maybe Nina would like to know what the classroom there is like.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I have my friends, and that's all I need.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: That's what Pasono said too.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Very well.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You're all brave little comrades. You will protect yourselves and each other, won't you?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Ms. Vila, I assure you SPDM is one of the safest places in the world.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: You don't have to worry.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The children will need to learn how to protect themselves sooner or later.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm only a teacher. I can't protect them forever.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila, aren't you coming with us?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Oh, but you're a Rusalka, so are you returning to the sea?
Surprise jumps across Vila's face.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What? No, never.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But will I be able to see you again if you turned into foam?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: How could foam be turned back into Vila again?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No, no, Avgust, I won't—won't turn into foam!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But you said the "eternal soul" is just another name. You said you don't have it, and the princess didn't have it either.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Pasono said the Rusalka princess turned into foam when she went to the sea.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: So, then you will—

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I will not, Avgust.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The "eternal soul" is nothing. It's only a name, something that could be given to anything. It doesn't have substance; you can't touch it or catch it.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: How can something you can't even touch turn me into foam? I haven't before, and I won't now.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Anyway, I won't be going back to the sea.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Then what is it? You said it can be everything, but also nothing?
Vila bends down, looking into Avgust's confused eyes.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I had the same thought at the beginning. That it could be anything I believed it to be, but maybe it didn't even exist at all.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I saw how barriers were broken and hate driven out from that town. That's why I thought "our Rayashki" was "eternal" and the people were all good "souls."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But now, I understand that's not true.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: What is true?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You are.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Me? Am I the "eternal soul"?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: No. Not you alone, but "all of you." You are the next generation of Rayashki, the survival of our people and our dreams, a future that will not be altered or reversed.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: As long as we have you, those who sacrificed themselves will never truly die, and ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The "eternal soul" will continue to exist for us and for them.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: So, for me, the "eternal soul" is nothing and everything.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Sounds a little like my arcane skill. Remember that sofa? It returned to a simple toy in only a few moments.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It's just a small trick, I'm afraid, far from "eternal."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Thanks for the example, Mr. Name Day.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Well, I can see that little Avgust is still very confused.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Perhaps I made it too complicated.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Did you understand what I mean, Comrade Avgust?
Avgust doesn't reply immediately. With him, it is never easy to tell whether he's fallen back into his own little world.
Or if he's piecing together something brilliant.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But if I can see it, how can it be nothing?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What do you mean, Avgust?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I don't think anyone has ever seen a soul.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: But I saw yours. It's golden, like the sun!
Vila turns to the direction Avgust showing her.
The morning sun has climbed high, spilling into the open corridor and stretching the silhouette of Vila's body.
Golden light surrounds her, outlining her shadow with a splash of warm yellow, a projection on a sparkling sea.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Ah ...
Then at the edge of her shadow, a familiar face.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Found her!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You're here, Ms. Vila!

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh, little Avgust is here too, and a gentleman that I'm afraid I don't know.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hello to you too!

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Oh, hello. You must be Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yes, that's right. I've come to prepare a lecture for the Far East branch.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Windsong!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Haha ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It is good to see you too, Ms. Windsong.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm certain the children will be happy that they can attend one of your lectures before they go to SPDM.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Now, let's go join the children.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Like we used to do.
